newsitem.title: UK: Dated sells lower, spreads narrow, Nigerian rises.
newsitem.headline: Dated sells lower, spreads narrow, Nigerian rises.

text.p: North Sea benchmark Dated Brent sold at a lower parity to November paper on Thursday, down 10 cents from its previous trade, taking CFDs lower.
Intermonth spreads also lost ground but other North Sea grades were stable in a market all but sold out of October crude.
Brent sold at Nov paper parity for an Oct 24-26 cargo. Today's Oct 25-27 date was kept by its equity holder.
Nov/Dec Brent narrowed to about +38 cents, Dec/Jan to just over +60 cents.
Nigerian crude differentials stayed buoyant despite lobbying from some crude contract holders ahead of next week's release by NNPC of term prices for November.
Nigerian values were helped by Taiwanese CPC's decision not to opt out of its term contract purchases from Elf for November despite the poor economics dictated by a very wide Brent/Dubai spread.
CPC will take two November VLCCS, shared three parts Forcados one part Angolan Palanca aboard one and three Forcados one Odudu on the second, traders said.
Korean Yukong might also have bought light Nigerian crude for end November loading to feed new refining capacity, traders said. But the purchase could not be confirmed.
Six cargoes of Qua Iboe already are committed to India in its November tender purchase.
Premiums over Brent were established at 70 cents for Bonny Light and Medium in a sale to a Spanish refiner on Wednesday.
Forcados, difficult to pin down in a secretive market, was put nearer to +80 cents.
The only possible dampener on rising premiums was the reversal in U.S. heating oil and European gas oil markets.
